make.name: Toyota
make.description: Japan's largest carmaker and a hybrid pioneer with the Prius. Its battery-electric history runs from the RAV4 EV of 1997 and the Tesla-powered RAV4 EV of 2012 to the bZ4X (now bZ) family, China-only bZ models built with BYD and GAC, and the 2025-2026 wave of C-HR+, Urban Cruiser and Highlander EVs.

models.name: RAV4 EV
models.description: Battery-electric version of the RAV4 sold mainly in California in two short runs: a nickel-metal-hydride first generation leased and sold from 1997 to 2003, and a second generation with a Tesla-built powertrain sold from 2012 until production ended in September 2014.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Fleet-lease EV with a 27 kWh NiMH pack and inductive Magne Charge charging; 328 units were sold to the public in 2002-2003 before the programme ended.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Tesla Motors supplied the 41.8 kWh lithium-ion pack and 115 kW motor; sold only in California, about 2,600 built.

models.name: iQ EV
models.description: Electric version of the tiny iQ city car, built in a run of about 100 for fleet and car-sharing use: sold as the Toyota eQ in Japan from December 2012 and as the Scion iQ EV in the US from March 2013.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Toyota iQ (eQ / Scion iQ EV)

generations.name: iQ EV
generations.description: 12 kWh lithium-ion pack and 47 kW motor; Toyota cut planned volume to about 100 cars.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Toyota iQ (eQ / Scion iQ EV)
Wikipedia: Toyota iQ (eQ / Scion iQ EV)

models.name: bZ4X
models.description: Toyota's first global battery-electric SUV, built on the e-TNGA platform shared with the Subaru Solterra and launched in mid-2022. A 2026 model-year refresh brought a 74.7 kWh pack, up to 338 hp, NACS charging and the name 'bZ' in North America and Ireland.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Launch version (US model years 2023-2025). FWD used a 71.4 kWh Panasonic-joint-venture pack; US AWD used a 72.8 kWh CATL pack limited to about 100 kW DC charging. China got its own 50.3/66.7 kWh CATL packs.

generations.name: Facelift (bZ)
generations.description: Mid-cycle refresh revealed in 2025: hammerhead nose, 57.7 or 74.7 kWh packs, silicon-carbide e-axles (up to 221 hp FWD, 338 hp AWD), battery preconditioning, 11 kW onboard charger and a NACS port in North America, where it is sold as the bZ.

sources.name: The Weekly Driver: 2026 bZ vs bZ Woodland

models.name: bZ Woodland
models.description: Longer, taller estate-style version of the refreshed bZ with standard AWD and roof rails, sold as the bZ Woodland in North America and the bZ4X Touring in Europe, Japan and Australia. Subaru sells it as the Trailseeker / E-Outback.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 140 mm longer and 20 mm taller than the bZ, single 74.7 kWh pack, 375 hp dual-motor AWD in North America.

sources.name: The Weekly Driver: 2026 bZ vs bZ Woodland
The Weekly Driver: 2026 bZ vs bZ Woodland

models.name: C-HR+
models.description: Compact electric crossover on the e-TNGA platform, unveiled in March 2025. Sold as the C-HR+ in Europe from late 2025 and as the C-HR (AWD only, 338 hp) in the US from 2026; Subaru sells it as the Uncharted.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 57.7 or 77 kWh packs in Europe; the US C-HR uses a 74.7 kWh pack with standard 338 hp dual-motor AWD and a NACS port.

models.name: C-HR EV
models.description: Battery-electric version of the first-generation C-HR built for China by GAC Toyota (C-HR EV) and FAW Toyota (IZOA EV), on sale from April 2020. The second-generation C-HR has no battery-electric version; the C-HR+ took that role.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Toyota C-HR (first generation China production 2018-2025)

generations.name: C-HR EV / IZOA EV
generations.description: 54.3 kWh pack, 150 kW front motor, 50 kW DC charging; NEDC range up to 400 km.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Toyota C-HR (C-HR EV / IZOA EV)
Wikipedia: Toyota C-HR (C-HR EV / IZOA EV)

models.name: bZ3
models.description: Compact electric sedan for China developed with BYD and built by FAW Toyota in Tianjin since 2023, using BYD Blade LFP batteries and BYD motors.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: BYD Blade LFP pack of 49.9 or 65.3 kWh; 135-180 kW front motor.

models.name: bZ3X
models.description: Affordable compact electric SUV developed with GAC and built by GAC Toyota; deliveries in China began in March 2025, and a right-hand-drive version reached Hong Kong and Macau in September 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: LFP packs of 50.03, 58 or 67.9 kWh with a 150 kW front motor; CLTC range 430-620 km.

models.name: bZ5
models.description: Coupe-styled compact electric SUV built by FAW Toyota with a BYD powertrain, shown as the bZ3C in 2024 and launched as the bZ5 in 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 200 kW BYD front motor, BYD Blade LFP packs of 65.28 or 73.98 kWh, CLTC range 550-630 km.

models.name: bZ7
models.description: Full-size electric sedan built by GAC Toyota on GAC's platform with a Huawei motor and HarmonyOS cockpit; launched in China on 29 March 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 207 kW Huawei DriveONE rear motor, CALB LFP packs of 71 or 88 kWh.

models.name: Urban Cruiser
models.description: Small electric SUV built by Suzuki in Gujarat, India, as Toyota's version of the Suzuki e Vitara. On sale in Europe and the UK from December 2025 and in India as the Urban Cruiser Ebella from May 2026.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Suzuki e Vitara / Toyota Urban Cruiser
Toyota UK media: Urban Cruiser UK sales launch

generations.name: First generation (BEV)
generations.description: BYD LFP packs of 49 or 61 kWh, front motor or dual-motor AWD, 67 kW DC charging.

models.name: C+pod
models.description: Two-seat ultra-compact electric car for Japan, sold first to companies and local governments from December 2020 and to private buyers from December 2021; discontinued in 2024.

generations.name: C+pod
generations.description: 9.06 kWh pack, 9.2 kW motor, 60 km/h top speed, 150 km WLTC (Class 1) range.

models.name: Hilux BEV
models.description: Battery-electric version of the ninth-generation Hilux pickup, launched in 2026 in markets including Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Australia (sold as the Hilux Travo-e in Thailand).

generations.name: Ninth generation BEV
generations.description: Dual-motor AWD with a 59.2 kWh pack; 240 km WLTP range.

models.name: Highlander
models.description: The fifth-generation Highlander, revealed in February 2026, is a three-row battery-electric SUV to be built in Georgetown, Kentucky. Toyota first targeted late 2026; as of September 2026 it says launch is in 2027, with reports of production starting no earlier than January 2027.

generations.name: Fifth generation
generations.description: First Toyota three-row EV: 77 or 95.8 kWh packs, FWD or AWD, NACS port. Toyota-estimated ranges only; no EPA rating or price yet.

models.name: Proace Electric
models.description: Electric version of the Proace mid-size van and Proace Verso people carrier, a Stellantis-built twin of the Citroen e-Jumpy / Peugeot e-Expert, sold in Europe since 2020-2021.

generations.name: Proace Electric
generations.description: Shared Stellantis eK0 drive: 100 kW motor with 50 or 75 kWh packs.

models.name: Proace City Electric
models.description: Electric version of the Proace City small van and Proace City Verso, a Stellantis-built twin of the Citroen e-Berlingo, unveiled in May 2021.

generations.name: Proace City Electric
generations.description: 100 kW motor with a 50 kWh-class pack; 330 km WLTP.

legacy_notes.note: Labelled bZ4X AWD (2023) but mixes trims: price $37,070 is the 2025 XLE FWD MSRP, EPA range 252 mi and battery 71.4 kWh are the FWD figures (US AWD: 72.8 kWh CATL pack, 228 mi), and 130 kW DC is wrong (US AWD about 100 kW). Mapped to the original-generation XLE AWD; the current model is the refreshed 2026 bZ.

Labelled bZ4X FWD (2023). Price $43,070 is the 2024 XLE FWD price; range 252 mi matches EPA. Mapped to original-generation XLE FWD. Model is still current but was refreshed and renamed 'bZ' in the US for 2026 (57.7/74.7 kWh, up to 338 hp, NACS).
